Expected reasoning: Requirement correctness versus behaviour under specified demand; expected results/response targets documented.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If a passing functional test proves capacity, add concurrent/repeated demand measurements.

Objective: Build: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Implement shared movement/bounds and appropriate Player/Hazard update overrides. Use supplied deterministic patrols and primitive geometry.
Check: Move each actor against a wall and call its update through the shared interface.
Expected reasoning: Wall preserves legal position; subclass behaviour differs appropriately; common bounds invariant holds.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If inheritance bypasses bounds, put/check shared behaviour in the appropriate common method.

Objective: Build: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Build once-only collection, lives, respawn/protection, score and active-play timer rules with the common fixed counts.
Check: Collect an item twice and collide during and at the end of protection; test pause across a timeout interval.
Expected reasoning: No duplicate collection; life/cooldown boundaries and active-time pause match contract.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If interval endpoints are unclear, state timestamps and expected lives before running.

Objective: Distinguish unit, integration, acceptance, regression and load testing.
Class activity: peer review an affected contract; focused retest/regression; version and restore evidence.
Check: A function changes its not-found result from -1 to None. Identify affected callers and regression tests.
Expected reasoning: Every caller interpreting result is reviewed; found index 0 remains valid; updated contract/test expectations documented.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If if result rejects index 0, use an explicit sentinel comparison.

Objective: Choose normal/boundary/rejected data and check expected state changes.
Class activity: developer impact/rights/responsibilities scenarios; user feedback and maintenance choices. Week 9 lessons 3–4 remain project workshops; week 10 project completion is unchanged.
Check: A developer copies a licensed library and ships user records in a demo. Identify separate rights/responsibility concerns.
Expected reasoning: Licence/attribution compliance and privacy/data minimisation both need review; public availability grants no blanket permission.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If attribution alone solves data exposure, separate code rights from personal-data handling.

Objective: Build: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Use the item-ID metadata dictionary and student-written linear search. Implement a taught sort for up to ten valid history scores without confusing record identity with position.
Check: Look up a known/missing item ID and sort [30,10,20,10] using the taught algorithm.
Expected reasoning: Lookup follows documented missing policy; result [10,10,20,30]; duplicates preserved; algorithm explained.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If dictionary lookup is claimed as authored linear search, demonstrate the separate traversal.

Objective: Build: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Connect map 1 completion to map 2, carry score/lives, refresh the 90-second map timer, and append one final score. Handle missing/malformed history and failed writes.
Check: Complete map 1 and then the game; show carried score/lives, fresh map time and exactly one final history append.
Expected reasoning: Transitions and persistence follow common FR7/FR10; redisplaying result does not append twice.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If map completion saves an extra final result, attach saving to the final-game transition.

Objective: Build: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Finish title/play/pause/result controls, readable feedback and full restart across both maps. Check relative paths and primitive asset fallbacks before freezing a test version.
Check: Pause, resume and restart from both maps, reading HUD values before/after each action.
Expected reasoning: Pause freezes gameplay; restart restores all initial fields/map/items; HUD only reflects state.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If some fields survive restart, compare every initial-state field with the contract.

Objective: Test: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Run unit/integration and shared acceptance tests, record actual state/output, repair one cause at a time and repeat earlier passing cases.
Check: Run one normal, one invalid and one boundary common test, then repeat a prior passing test after repair.
Expected reasoning: Expected/actual results and FR/NFR links retained; regression checks demonstrate unchanged earlier behaviour.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If failure evidence is erased, preserve original and repaired build IDs/results.

Objective: Acceptance: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Use a peer instruction-only trial and the common reliability/usability/response checks on the nominated school setup. Record limitations, source/asset checks and retests.
Check: On the declared school PC, record response observations and a colour/sound-independent player trial.
Expected reasoning: Measured method/results and player feedback are actual, not inferred from FPS; limitations acknowledged.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If no physical input was observed, leave that check pending and run the visible-window trial.

Objective: Evaluate: connect the shared game requirements to an observable outcome.
Class activity: Explain the actor hierarchy, independent maps, dictionary, student search/sort and file policy. Restore a saved version and hand over evidence, evaluation and retrospective.
Check: Restore the submitted version separately and demonstrate one met and one incomplete requirement.
Expected reasoning: Restored build runs; independent explanation uses tests and honest limitations; improvement prioritised.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only latest working copy exists, establish version identity before claiming restoration.

Objective: Compare all seven OSI layers with the four-layer DoD TCP/IP model.
Class activity: retrieve Year 11 network knowledge; compare OSI/TCP-IP functions; assemble encapsulation units and explain boundaries.
Check: Contrast IP and MAC roles across a routed path; identify which addresses change at ordinary forwarding hops.
Expected reasoning: Destination IP identifies remote host; local link headers/MACs change per hop under no-NAT assumption.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If remote server MAC is used locally, identify the first-hop gateway MAC.

Objective: Trace encapsulation, local link forwarding and routed IP traffic.
Class activity: ports/DNS/gateway/ARP; trace the two-LAN route; explain layer 2 switching and layer 3 routing with changed/unchanged fields.
Check: Explain DNS, port number, default gateway and ARP during an IPv4 web request.
Expected reasoning: DNS maps name; port identifies service endpoint; gateway routes remote traffic; ARP resolves local next-hop IPv4 to MAC.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If DNS is called routing, trace name resolution before packet delivery.

Objective: Compare TCP/UDP behaviour, header fields and sequence/acknowledgement meaning.
Class activity: compare TCP/UDP services and header architecture; desk-check connection and byte acknowledgements; justify scenarios.
Check: Compare TCP/UDP delivery and explain one header field's purpose in each.
Expected reasoning: TCP ordered reliable stream with sequence/acknowledgement; UDP datagrams with ports/length/checksum semantics as taught.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If both guarantee delivery, explain application handling after a lost UDP datagram.

Objective: Calculate model packet/frame lengths and justify protocol choices.
Class activity: packet/frame sizing and padding; unfamiliar trace/fault diagnosis; workbook feedback and retrieval. Four lessons in week 11; no new network project.
Check: An illustrative packet has 20-byte IP +20-byte TCP headers and 10-byte data. Find packet size; add 18-byte Ethernet header/FCS and padding.
Expected reasoning: IP packet 50 bytes; frame 68 excluding preamble/gap; payload exceeds 46-byte minimum so no padding.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If packet and frame sizes are conflated, draw encapsulation boundaries and list counted fields.

Objective: Distinguish RFC 1918 private space from public and special-purpose addresses.
Class activity: retrieve IP/MAC/gateway roles; IPv4/IPv6 and address scope; convert prefixes and masks.
Check: A host is 192.168.6.10/24; remote service 203.0.113.8. What IP and local next-hop destination are used?
Expected reasoning: Remote destination IP remains service; frame targets local gateway MAC, resolved locally.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If gateway replaces destination IP, separate packet header from link frame.

Objective: Convert IPv4 prefixes/masks and find network, broadcast and ordinary host ranges.
Class activity: bitwise AND, block boundaries and /27 worked range; transfer to /20 and local/remote gateway checks.
Check: For 192.168.6.77/27, calculate network, broadcast, usable range and ordinary host capacity.
Expected reasoning: Network .64, broadcast .95, usable .65–.94, 30 hosts; block size 32.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If .77 is the network, apply mask or locate the containing block boundary.

Objective: Choose aligned, non-overlapping subnets and validate gateway allocations.
Class activity: equal-size versus variable-length subnetting; four-group capacity/alignment/non-overlap plan and feedback.
Check: Allocate 50 and 20 ordinary hosts within 192.168.10.0/24 using largest-first VLSM.
Expected reasoning: For example .0/26 (62 usable), .64/27 (30); aligned non-overlapping blocks, gateways included in requirements.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If /27 is used for 50, compare usable capacity before allocation.

Objective: Compare IPv4/IPv6 notation and explain the limits of the ordinary IPv4 host formula.
Class activity: IPv6 expansion/compression, addressing scenario diagnosis and independent plan verification. Four lessons in week 12; no extra network project.
Check: Expand 2001:db8::1 and explain one IPv6 difference from ordinary IPv4 subnet broadcasts.
Expected reasoning: 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001; IPv6 uses multicast rather than broadcast.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If :: is expanded to a fixed count regardless of context, count the eight total hextets.

Objective: Select components and media for stated requirements.
Class activity: requirements and components; interpret physical/logical topology; identify Cisco symbols and redraw the example.
Check: A remote site needs connectivity, segmented access and a stated user load. Choose components against those requirements.
Expected reasoning: Roles and quantities follow traffic/security/load needs; no unsupported product-brand recommendation.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If components are listed without reasons, map each to one requirement and traffic path.

Objective: Draw physical/logical topology with addressing, segmentation and specified diagram conventions.
Class activity: VLANs/broadcast domains, gateways and service policy; test the simplified offline traffic matrix.
Check: Explain why two VLANs require suitable routing and access policy for approved inter-VLAN traffic.
Expected reasoning: Separate broadcast domains; router/L3 function connects them; policy permits only required services.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If VLAN alone is called encryption, distinguish segmentation from confidentiality.

Objective: Explain broadcast domains and service-specific filtering.
Class activity: demand/bottleneck calculations, media/topology tradeoffs and capacity feedback.
Check: Forty clients each demand 8 Mb/s across a 200 Mb/s uplink. Calculate shortfall and justify a revision.
Expected reasoning: Demand 320 Mb/s, shortfall at least 120 before overhead; capacity upgrade or controlled concurrency justified.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If 200/40 is called required demand, separate available share from each client's requirement.

Objective: Calculate bottlenecks and interpret ping/traceroute evidence.
Class activity: interpret synthetic logs, practice ping/tracert in the assigned lab, evaluate and revise the design. Four lessons in week 13; practical work is embedded.
Check: A ping fails but an application works. What can and cannot be concluded? Propose a next scoped check.
Expected reasoning: ICMP may be filtered; failure does not prove host/service down; compare permitted application/route/DNS evidence.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If ping proves a cause, name an alternative and an observation distinguishing it.

Objective: Trace structures, aliases and object state.
Class activity: closed-note diagnostic, confidence record and guided programming/state/algorithm correction.
Check: Trace a two-object mutation and a duplicate-key dictionary update without running code.
Expected reasoning: Only intended independent object changes; dictionary replaces existing-key value; explain state ownership.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If both objects change, inspect shared references and test a deep-enough independent construction.

Objective: Choose algorithms from their contracts and repair boundary faults.
Class activity: integrated network case, diagram/policy/capacity reasoning and evidence interpretation.
Check: For a new network case, link one diagram path, access rule and capacity calculation to supplied facts.
Expected reasoning: All three use the same hosts/services/load; conclusion acknowledges missing evidence.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If a generic design is copied, label changed addresses and demand before reasoning.

Objective: Apply addressing, topology, policy and capacity reasoning to a shared scenario.
Class activity: 40-minute original controlled practice, followed by initial marking and feedback.
Check: After the 40-minute practice, identify one unanswered subpart and one result you can justify independently.
Expected reasoning: Original responses retained; gap classified and evidence distinguished from confidence.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If correction replaces attempt, retain both and date the supported work.

Objective: Use test evidence and corrected attempts to set revision priorities.
Class activity: corrections, fresh transfer tasks and two evidence-based revision priorities. Four lessons in week 14; no additional project.
Check: Repair one programming and one networking error, then answer a fresh variation of each.
Expected reasoning: Fresh outputs/ranges/decisions recomputed from changed facts; two specific priorities follow.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only the answer wording changes, change input values and retest the reasoning.

Objective: Choose precise revision priorities from errors and confidence.
Class activity: retrieve week 14 evidence, attempt baseline questions and choose one programming plus one networking priority.
Check: Use prior evidence to choose one programming and one networking priority; state a diagnostic result for each.
Expected reasoning: Priority references an actual incorrect trace/test/range and an observable target.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If selection is based only on preference, attempt a short unseen case first.

Objective: Transfer state, algorithm and object reasoning to unfamiliar examples.
Class activity: two targeted stations, teacher feedback and explained correction; extensions for secure skills.
Check: At each chosen station, show the first incorrect reasoning step and a corrected independent case.
Expected reasoning: Cause, correction and changed-case result recorded separately.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only final answer is compared, trace intermediate state or subnet boundary.

Objective: Apply subnetting, capacity and policy reasoning with stated limits.
Class activity: fresh mixed transfer, marking and correction within the same lesson.
Check: In a fresh case, combine a safe empty-list search result with an ordinary /28 subnet range.
Expected reasoning: Empty search returns contract sentinel; /28 has 16 addresses/14 ordinary usable hosts with aligned boundaries.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If subnet result is guessed, apply mask and verify network/broadcast endpoints.

Objective: Document independent retries and practical evidence still needed.
Class activity: delayed retries, mixed retrieval and a concrete week 16 revision plan. Four lessons in week 15; no additional project.
Check: Retry an earlier weak skill after a gap and plan one specific week-16 action from the result.
Expected reasoning: Independent delayed response and next task/resource/time are recorded; unresolved support need remains visible.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If immediate repetition is called delayed evidence, schedule another later changed case.

Objective: Distinguish Unit 3 practice from the full Year 12 examination.
Class activity: assessment scope, commands, pacing and worked trace/contract rehearsal.
Check: Explain how 'compare' differs from 'identify', then outline a short-answer time/checking plan.
Expected reasoning: Compare addresses similarities/differences against criteria; identify names; timing follows practice scope and school instructions.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If compare gives two unrelated definitions, add an explicit relationship using the same criterion.

Objective: Plan written evidence for trace, explain, justify and evaluate tasks.
Class activity: teacher setup, 40-minute original practice and initial reflection.
Check: After the original practice attempt, flag one uncertain answer and justify one trace without consulting its key.
Expected reasoning: Original timed response and independent reasoning retained; uncertainty is specific.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If certainty is inferred from finishing early, inspect each command/subpart.

Objective: Attempt and mark an original timed sample.
Class activity: point-based marking, error diagnosis and targeted correction.
Check: For one missed criterion, classify cause and write a repair that changes the underlying reasoning.
Expected reasoning: Original mismatch supports cause; corrected trace/algorithm/network argument addresses it.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If correction is copied text, explain the step orally with changed facts.

Objective: Verify correction through fresh retries and a final revision plan.
Class activity: fresh independent retries, final readiness checklist and revision plan. Four lessons in week 16; weeks 17–18 remain blocked for examinations.
Check: Complete a fresh programming retry and network retry, then name evidence and remaining limitations in your readiness plan.
Expected reasoning: Results are independent and scenario-specific; school confirms actual exam requirements; no score guarantees.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If readiness is only a percentage, name which skills remain untested.

Objective: Identify anomalies and functional dependencies in a flat relation.
Class activity: retrieve relational/normalisation foundations; diagnose the flat booking relation and state dependencies.
Check: LoanID→EquipmentID→EquipmentName. Identify the transitive dependency and an update anomaly.
Expected reasoning: EquipmentName depends through EquipmentID; repeated name updates can conflict across loans.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If LoanID→EquipmentID is called partial, first check whether the key is composite.

Objective: Read/create crow’s-foot relationships and resolve many-to-many with a composite bridge.
Class activity: read six-table crow’s-foot model, composite bridge and optional one-to-one; write notation.
Check: A Booking(MemberID,SessionID) may have one Attendance record. Explain the composite reference and optional participation.
Expected reasoning: Attendance references both booking-key parts; booking has zero/one attendance, each attendance one booking.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only MemberID is linked, test one member booking two sessions.

Objective: Represent optional one-to-one attendance and its paired foreign key.
Class activity: dictionary/integrity/schema reconciliation; predict and check constraints in an offline database.
Check: A required FK permits NULL in SQLite unless constrained. Reconcile a mandatory Session→Workshop relationship.
Expected reasoning: WorkshopID uses NOT NULL plus enforced FK; dictionary/ER minimum and schema agree.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If FK alone is assumed sufficient, test null and nonexistent IDs separately.

Objective: Reconcile a data dictionary with SQLite enforcement and remaining business rules.
Class activity: independent exhibition-model transfer and explained feedback. Four lessons in semester week 1; no extra project.
Check: Model Artist,Exhibit,Visitor,Reservation,CheckIn,Venue from the exhibition task and justify one bridge constraint.
Expected reasoning: Six distinct roles; Reservation resolves visitor/exhibit many-to-many with unique pair; CheckIn references the pair.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If six arbitrary tables are created, map every entity and key to a stated requirement.

Objective: Write four-table inner joins using declared keys.
Class activity: retrieve schema/keys and predict four-table joins.
Check: A booking joins one member, one session and one workshop. Predict one row per booking and explain the key chain.
Expected reasoning: Booking→Member by MemberID; Booking→Session by SessionID; Session→Workshop by WorkshopID; required references yield one match each.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If names are joined, test equal labels and retain identifiers.

Objective: Use aggregates/GROUP BY and distinguish row/group filters.
Class activity: implement joins/aliases and diagnose missing conditions.
Check: Two bookings and three members are joined with no ON condition. Predict the cross-product row count and repair the link.
Expected reasoning: Six combinations; use declared MemberID key match; aliases do not create joins automatically.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If DISTINCT is proposed first, repair the relationship before considering output duplicates.

Objective: Create calculated and concatenated fields with aliases.
Class activity: aggregate at session/booking grain; grouped inner reports.
Check: A session capacity 2 has two bookings. Explain why summing capacity after that join yields 4.
Expected reasoning: Capacity repeats per booking; aggregate at session grain to count its two places once.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If SUM(DISTINCT Capacity) is the universal fix, add another session with capacity 2.

Objective: Diagnose zero-count, composite-key and multiplied-total errors.
Class activity: zero-booking LEFT JOIN/count clinic and feedback.
Check: S1 has two bookings; S2 has none. Compare COUNT(*) and COUNT(childKey) after a LEFT JOIN.
Expected reasoning: S1 gives 2/2; S2 gives 1/0; preserved NULL child row is not a booking.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If zero session disappears, start from Session and inspect filters on child fields.

Objective: Write four-table inner joins using declared keys.
Class activity: calculated percentages, concatenated labels and aliases.
Check: For capacity 3 and one booking, calculate remaining places and fill percentage to one decimal. Why use 100.0?
Expected reasoning: 2 places, 33.3%; real arithmetic avoids integer truncation; alias labels result without changing stored schema.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If percentage is zero, inspect integer division before rounding.

Objective: Use aggregates/GROUP BY and distinguish row/group filters.
Class activity: composite attendance joins, NULL and row/group filtering.
Check: Attendance for M1/S1 exists but M1/S2 is missing. Why must both key parts join, and what does missing Present mean?
Expected reasoning: Both identify the booking; missing attendance is NULL/unknown, not recorded absence 0; WHERE/HAVING act at different stages.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If absence is inferred, distinguish missing record from an explicit false value.

Objective: Create calculated and concatenated fields with aliases.
Class activity: repair multiplied totals and independently test changed data.
Check: Two sessions each have capacity 2. Why is SUM(DISTINCT Capacity)=2 wrong for total places, and how should it be calculated?
Expected reasoning: Distinct removes equal values, not duplicate entities; total is 4 at session grain.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If a join still multiplies totals, aggregate sessions independently before combining reports.

Objective: Diagnose zero-count, composite-key and multiplied-total errors.
Class activity: fresh report transfer, expected/actual evidence and feedback. Eight lessons across two weeks; no additional project.
Check: Add the first booking to an unbooked session. Predict changes to its count/remaining/fill report, then run it.
Expected reasoning: Count increases 0→1; remaining decreases one; percentage recomputed from its capacity; other sessions unchanged.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If all rows change, inspect join/filter scope and compare target/non-target evidence.

Objective: Implement a scoped six-table database and required reports.
Class activity: controlled CREATE/ALTER/data changes and rollback lab.
Check: Contrast CREATE, ALTER, UPDATE and ROLLBACK in a disposable database, checking before/after state.
Expected reasoning: Create structure, alter structure, change records, undo uncommitted transaction changes; committed data not magically undone.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If rollback restores any history, mark the transaction boundary and commit point.

Objective: Clean/import data with documented decisions and rollback.
Class activity: source mapping/cleaning and data-quality decisions.
Check: An import contains duplicate IDs, blank required names and ambiguous dates. State a defensible policy for each.
Expected reasoning: Use source evidence; reject/quarantine unresolved rows; preserve provenance and do not invent values.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If blanks are filled by guessing, record uncertainty and ask for authoritative source clarification.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: transaction/ACID and parameterised booking reasoning.
Check: A booking requires two inserts. Explain atomicity on second-insert failure and why SQL parameters matter.
Expected reasoning: Rollback both changes; parameters separate data from SQL syntax; atomicity does not itself validate all business rules.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If first insert remains, add explicit transaction/error handling and negative test.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: test design, backup/recovery and project preparation.
Check: Design a failed-write test and a backup recovery test before the project starts.
Expected reasoning: Expected failure preserves valid data; restore into safe target and query known contents; actual evidence later recorded.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If backup creation is called recovery, include reopening and content verification.

Objective: Implement a scoped six-table database and required reports.
Class activity: Investigate the booking database brief and scope.
Check: Translate one database-project need into a measurable functional criterion and one quality criterion.
Expected reasoning: Operation/result and measurable quality are tied to brief, not table count alone.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If criteria say 'secure' or 'fast', specify access result or named-condition response measure.

Objective: Clean/import data with documented decisions and rollback.
Class activity: Design the six-table model and key relationships.
Check: Trace the project's six-table design from Member to Booking to Session to Workshop and justify cardinalities.
Expected reasoning: Declared keys and business rules support the links; optional records and unique pairs distinguished.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If cardinalities come from sample row counts, return to the stated business rules.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: Specify the dictionary, constraints and transaction requirements.
Check: Specify PK/FK/null/domain rules and the transaction boundary for a booking operation.
Expected reasoning: Dictionary matches schema; related writes commit/rollback together; cross-row capacity rule explicitly handled separately.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If a CHECK is assumed to count all bookings, distinguish row constraints from aggregate rules.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: Desk-check the design and agree acceptance criteria.
Check: Desk-check duplicate booking and unavailable-capacity cases; agree their expected database state.
Expected reasoning: Rejected operations leave no partial booking/attendance changes; criteria identify the enforcing mechanism.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If every failure expects an exception, document the actual chosen error/report contract.

Objective: Apply CIA to specific assets/consequences.
Class activity: retrieve threat vocabulary, CIA/AAA worked case and mechanism classification; choose justified evidence.
Check: A shared account exports records and alters capacity. Apply CIA and AAA to the case.
Expected reasoning: Confidentiality/integrity affected; availability considered separately; shared identity/permissions/log attribution limit AAA.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If CIA/AAA are only expanded, link each applicable term to observed or plausible effects.

Objective: Distinguish authentication, authorisation and accounting.
Class activity: synthetic log/case analysis, hypotheses and alternatives, manual/offline counts and explained feedback.
Check: Three failed logins precede a successful export from one IP. Give two hypotheses and one discriminating observation.
Expected reasoning: Attack and legitimate user error are possible; identity/session/authorised audit evidence needed; IP alone not a person.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If compromise is declared proven, state what the log does not establish.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: Create the six-table database and verify integrity constraints.
Check: Create the project schema and attempt one valid insert plus duplicate/null/orphan failures.
Expected reasoning: Named constraints enforced on the actual connection; valid state remains after rejected operations.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If SQLite foreign keys are assumed on, verify PRAGMA on the connection used.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: Implement core reports with expected/actual results.
Check: Run one core report against a manually predicted fixture including an unbooked session.
Expected reasoning: Expected rows/counts include zero correctly; actual output compared and non-target rows checked.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only SQL execution success is recorded, calculate expected content independently.

Objective: Compare logs, anti-malware, firewalls, ACLs, IPS, VPN and people/physical controls.
Class activity: control purpose/limits, ordered traffic rules and scoped role permissions; manual/offline predictions.
Check: An ordered firewall rule permits staff HTTPS then denies others. Predict a staff match and a guest match; distinguish network rule from app role.
Expected reasoning: First matching rule governs as specified; network traffic permission does not grant application editing rights.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If a port allow permits every action, add server-side operation authorisation.

Objective: Predict ordered traffic rules and scoped role permissions.
Class activity: response scenarios, positive/negative acceptance tests, competing proposals and explained feedback.
Check: Test an authorised capacity change and a denied student change; specify expected state and response.
Expected reasoning: Staff change succeeds within rules; student request rejected server-side with capacity unchanged; both outcomes logged appropriately.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If button hiding is the only test, send/check the prohibited operation at the enforcement boundary.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: Implement safe changes and parameterised operations.
Check: Implement a parameterised project update with an exact target condition and test quote-containing data.
Expected reasoning: Data stays data, intended row changes, non-target rows preserved; validation/permission checks remain separate.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If input is concatenated into SQL, replace it with placeholders and bound parameters.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: Test positive and negative transaction cases.
Check: Force the second step of a transaction to fail; verify that no first-step write remains committed.
Expected reasoning: All-or-none behaviour demonstrated by queries; rollback followed by usable connection/state.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only an error message is checked, inspect database contents after failure.

Objective: Compare historical ciphers and modern symmetric/public-key roles.
Class activity: historical ciphers, key roles and fingerprints; predict/run/explain the offline Python activity.
Check: Contrast encryption, hashing and a historical substitution cipher in purpose and limitations.
Expected reasoning: Encryption reversible with key; hash digest comparison one-way by design; historical cipher is weak teaching model.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If hash is called decryptable ciphertext, distinguish recoverability from comparison.

Objective: Distinguish encryption, hashes, signatures and key agreement.
Class activity: certificate cards, TLS ordering and connection-risk explanation.
Check: Order certificate checking, authenticated key agreement and symmetric record protection in simplified TLS 1.3.
Expected reasoning: Certificate binds identity/key; handshake proves key possession/authenticates agreement; derived symmetric keys protect records; no RSA key transport claim.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If public-key encryption is used for every record, separate handshake authentication from bulk encryption.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: Implement atomic booking and attendance behaviour.
Check: Implement atomic booking plus attendance behaviour and test both existing and missing related records.
Expected reasoning: Contract permits only valid linked state; unique pair/reference checks enforced; success commits consistently.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If a missing attendance record means absent, preserve unknown/not-recorded semantics.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: Test failed operations and rollback outcomes.
Check: Reject a duplicate booking or invalid attendance link and inspect every affected table after rollback.
Expected reasoning: No partial changes remain; pre-existing rows unchanged; exact failure cause and expected response recorded.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If memory state alone is checked, query the actual database after failure.

Objective: Apply APP 5, 8, 10, 11 and 12 with explicit entity and jurisdiction assumptions.
Class activity: entity/jurisdiction, five APPs and breach cases; manual predictions and explained feedback.
Check: Before applying APPs or breach rules, identify entity, jurisdiction, date and missing eligibility facts.
Expected reasoning: Applicable law cannot be inferred from 'school' alone; distinguish federal/state scope and current commencement dates; assess facts promptly.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If 30 days is treated as automatic notification delay, revisit assessment versus notification obligations.

Objective: Distinguish a suspected incident, an eligible federal breach and WA commencement dates.
Class activity: data-mining critique, paper red/blue-team scope and source/project decisions.
Check: A data-mining proposal reuses records beyond their stated purpose; a red team seeks broader targets. Give one justified limit each.
Expected reasoning: Purpose/consent/authority and minimisation checked; testing remains within explicit written scope; defensive role does not grant unlimited access.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If public availability means unrestricted reuse, inspect purpose, permissions and affected people.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: Map and clean import data using source evidence.
Check: Map a raw import row to schema fields, recording one cleaning change and one unresolved uncertainty.
Expected reasoning: Traceable original→clean value with rule/source; uncertainty quarantined rather than invented.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If normalisation is confused with cleaning, separate relational design from correcting source values.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: Test all-or-none import and recovery; preserve decision logs.
Check: Import a batch containing one invalid required row under an all-or-none policy, then test recovery safely.
Expected reasoning: Entire batch rejected/rolled back as contracted; previous valid records survive; restore/reopen result checked.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If valid prefix rows remain, widen transaction boundary to the complete batch.

Objective: Implement a scoped six-table database and required reports.
Class activity: Run the full acceptance suite and inspect failures.
Check: Run the full project acceptance suite and select the highest-impact actual failure for investigation.
Expected reasoning: Requirement-linked results identify real failures; priority follows user impact/dependencies, not ease alone.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If unrun tests are marked pass, change them to pending and execute them.

Objective: Clean/import data with documented decisions and rollback.
Class activity: Repair, restore/reopen and run regression checks.
Check: After repairing one defect, restore/reopen a separate database and rerun relevant regression checks.
Expected reasoning: Repair and recovery are distinct; known records/reports persist as expected; earlier passing behaviour retained.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If in-memory rollback proves persistence, close/reopen the actual file and inspect it.

Objective: Use transactions and parameters while distinguishing application rules from constraints.
Class activity: Demonstrate independent implementation and justify decisions.
Check: Demonstrate one transaction, one report and one rejected unauthorised operation, explaining your implementation.
Expected reasoning: Student links code/schema to observed outcomes; no claim that demonstration alone proves production security.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If reference code is recited, change a fixture and explain the new outcome independently.

Objective: Test, recover and evaluate against measurable requirements.
Class activity: Evaluate against requirements and submit evidence.
Check: Evaluate the database against two met and one incomplete criterion and rank a realistic improvement.
Expected reasoning: Judgements cite actual tests and limitations; handover includes setup/recovery guidance and remaining risks.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If evaluation lists features only, connect each criterion to evidence and user effect.

Objective: Apply keys, dependencies and integrity rules to a changed six-table case.
Class activity: key/dependency/diagram retrieval and design repair.
Check: Repair an ER design that duplicates CategoryName in every Equipment row; identify the dependency and keys.
Expected reasoning: CategoryID→CategoryName separated; Equipment retains FK; anomaly explained and cardinalities preserved.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only a diagram is redrawn, show which update inconsistency is removed.

Objective: Write and debug joins, grouping, calculated fields and NULL-aware reports.
Class activity: manual report prediction, independent SQL and NULL/grain feedback.
Check: Predict LEFT JOIN counts for two parents with 2 and 0 children, then write the grouped SQL.
Expected reasoning: Counts 2/0 using non-null child key; grouping at parent ID; deterministic order if required.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If zero becomes one, inspect outer-join placeholder versus actual child key.

Objective: Explain transactions, connectivity, recovery and justified security/privacy decisions.
Class activity: transactions, connectivity and recovery evidence.
Check: Explain what evidence distinguishes rollback, successful backup and successful recovery; name a connectivity layer involved.
Expected reasoning: Rollback undoes uncommitted changes; backup copies data; recovery restores and verifies contents; driver/API connects application to DBMS as taught.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If all are 'save', trace failure/recovery sequence with state checkpoints.

Objective: Attempt controlled practice and demonstrate transfer after explained feedback.
Class activity: security/cryptography/privacy case response with brief Unit 3 retrieval.
Check: For an unauthorised export over HTTPS, distinguish transport protection, authorisation and breach evidence; recall a routed next hop.
Expected reasoning: HTTPS protects transport but not permission; export facts need scope/identity/impact assessment; remote packet uses gateway locally.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If encryption is said to authorise export, separate identity/permission from channel security.

Objective: Apply keys, dependencies and integrity rules to a changed six-table case.
Class activity: changed-data query transfer and explanation.
Check: Add a zero-booking session and a second equal-capacity session; predict effect on counts and total capacity.
Expected reasoning: New session remains in all-session report with 0; each distinct session's capacity counts once even when equal.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If DISTINCT removes one capacity, aggregate by session identity instead.

Objective: Write and debug joins, grouping, calculated fields and NULL-aware reports.
Class activity: unfamiliar model and evidence-based extended response.
Check: For an unfamiliar model, explain a composite relationship and justify one constraint with a counterexample.
Expected reasoning: Both key parts preserve the intended relationship; counterexample shows invalid state prevented by constraint.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If table count substitutes for design, return to the relationship's business rule.

Objective: Explain transactions, connectivity, recovery and justified security/privacy decisions.
Class activity: original controlled formative sample in the existing theory-test slot; teacher adaptation required for summative use.
Check: After the controlled sample is collected, identify one answer that needed source facts and one with an untested assumption.
Expected reasoning: Original evidence retained; facts and assumptions separated without changing assessment conditions.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If plausible inference is presented as observation, label the missing evidence.

Objective: Attempt controlled practice and demonstrate transfer after explained feedback.
Class activity: marking, explained correction, fresh independent retry and consolidation priorities.
Check: Repair one missed criterion and attempt a changed case before selecting consolidation priorities.
Expected reasoning: New case changes data/requirements; response demonstrates reasoning rather than copied key text.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If priority is vague, name a precise SQL, design or security operation to retry.

Objective: Diagnose gaps across Year 12 strands and revisit earlier prerequisites.
Class activity: diagnostic, prior-evidence review and two priorities.
Check: Choose two priorities from the diagnostic, each supported by an incorrect original response and a success criterion.
Expected reasoning: Actual evidence determines priorities; criterion is demonstrable by a fresh answer/test.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If confidence alone determines choice, attempt the related unseen diagnostic first.

Objective: Repair Python/algorithm/object behaviour and database query/model reasoning.
Class activity: programming/algorithm/object repair clinic and independent practice.
Check: Trace a dictionary accumulator on [('A',2),('B',0),('A',3)] and state its empty-input result.
Expected reasoning: {'A':5,'B':0}; empty {}; initialise missing keys safely and preserve input.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If repeated A overwrites 2, add to previous total rather than replacing it.

Objective: Explain network/security/privacy decisions using requirements and evidence.
Class activity: fresh database design/SQL/transaction repair clinic.
Check: Write a safe update for one row and a failed second-step transaction test; explain expected unchanged state on failure.
Expected reasoning: Parameters and exact predicate target intended row; rollback leaves no partial writes; existing rows verified.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If WHERE alone is considered safe, test its actual target and authorisation separately.

Objective: Record fresh and delayed retries, then plan remaining exam preparation.
Class activity: networking/security/responsibility clinic and explanation.
Check: Explain a /27 host range, least privilege and one privacy uncertainty in a supplied case.
Expected reasoning: Aligned /27 has 30 ordinary usable hosts; permissions limited to needed actions; legal conclusion depends on entity/date/facts.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If definitive legal outcome is guessed, record missing scope facts and appropriate source check.

Objective: Diagnose gaps across Year 12 strands and revisit earlier prerequisites.
Class activity: priority 1 repair and changed independent attempt.
Check: For priority 1, change one input or requirement and solve the resulting task without the old answer visible.
Expected reasoning: Changed facts produce recomputed output/design/reasoning; original and fresh results both retained.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If wording alone changes, alter a boundary value or relationship and retry.

Objective: Repair Python/algorithm/object behaviour and database query/model reasoning.
Class activity: priority 2 repair and changed independent attempt.
Check: For priority 2, give a counterexample to your former wrong rule, then solve a new case.
Expected reasoning: Counterexample exposes the misconception; fresh solution applies a corrected rule explicitly.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If counterexample also fits the wrong rule, choose a boundary or missing-data case that distinguishes them.

Objective: Explain network/security/privacy decisions using requirements and evidence.
Class activity: mixed transfer and evidence-based feedback.
Check: Combine one algorithm trace, one report prediction and one justified control in a new scenario.
Expected reasoning: All answers use supplied data and stated contracts; uncertainty or unavailable facts are explicit.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If examples are memorised, change names/values while keeping the underlying concept.

Objective: Record fresh and delayed retries, then plan remaining exam preparation.
Class activity: delayed retries, remaining support and Weeks 15–16 revision plan.
Check: Retry both priorities after a gap; plan one action for each remaining weakness in Weeks 15–16.
Expected reasoning: Dated independent evidence supports demonstrated/needs-retry/not-yet-evidenced judgements.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If all are called mastered after reading, require a changed independent attempt.

Objective: Read current instructions and plan lesson-size mixed practice.
Class activity: current instructions, command/source use and pacing plan.
Check: Explain the difference between 'analyse' and 'identify'; locate a source fact and plan a practice time budget.
Expected reasoning: Analysis connects parts/evidence to conclusions; identification names; source fact is cited and pacing fits local practice scope.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If generic definitions replace source use, link a specific fact to one conclusion.

Objective: Apply Python, database, network and security knowledge to supplied facts.
Class activity: original Set A timed attempt.
Check: After Set A, identify one unfinished subpart and preserve one uncertain original response before seeing the key.
Expected reasoning: Original attempt/time and uncertainty recorded; supported corrections remain separate.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If answers were revealed first, label support and select a fresh independent task.

Objective: Mark criteria, explain errors and demonstrate changed independent retries.
Class activity: criterion marking, explained corrections and targeted repair.
Check: Explain why one Set A criterion was missed, then repair its reasoning with an explicit calculation or causal link.
Expected reasoning: Cause follows original response; repair uses source facts and correct method, not score alone.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If only the model sentence is copied, explain the same point with a changed figure.

Objective: Use evidence and teacher feedback for a manageable readiness plan.
Class activity: fresh retries and short revision plan.
Check: Complete one fresh retry from Set A weaknesses and schedule one later retry with a specific resource.
Expected reasoning: Changed-case answer and success check show progress; remaining limitations recorded.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If the same answer is repeated immediately, change the task and revisit after a gap.

Objective: Read current instructions and plan lesson-size mixed practice.
Class activity: original Set B timed attempt.
Check: After Set B, record one answer needing a trace and one needing justified judgement; check every command/subpart.
Expected reasoning: Original responses retained; appropriate evidence form chosen for each; no new full-paper claim.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If all answers are definitions, match each command to its required reasoning.

Objective: Apply Python, database, network and security knowledge to supplied facts.
Class activity: marking and specific cause repair.
Check: Classify one Set B error and show the exact step where source interpretation or technical reasoning failed.
Expected reasoning: Content/interpretation/tracing/time diagnosis is supported by original work and a precise correction.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If every mistake is called careless, name the missing operation or fact.

Objective: Mark criteria, explain errors and demonstrate changed independent retries.
Class activity: unfamiliar mixed transfer and later priority retry.
Check: Solve an unfamiliar changed case from a prior weakness and compare it with your delayed retry evidence.
Expected reasoning: Independent response uses new data; comparison shows what transfers and any remaining support.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If old expected values are reused, recalculate from the changed stimulus.

Objective: Use evidence and teacher feedback for a manageable readiness plan.
Class activity: delayed retrieval, readiness/support plan and instruction/materials check.
Check: Without notes, retry two selected weak skills and state remaining support plus official exam arrangements to confirm.
Expected reasoning: Readiness rests on dated independent work; school confirms venue/materials/access arrangements; no guaranteed grade inferred.
Follow-up if not yet secure: If checklist ticks replace evidence, attach the actual fresh responses and unresolved questions.
